content: Methylcellulose is an over-the-counter (OTC) laxative approved by the FDA for the treatment of constipation. It is commonly used to help restore and maintain regular bowel movements and to relieve constipation, including cases associated with other bowel disorders such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), when recommended by a physician. Typically, it produces a bowel movement within 12 to 72 hours. When taking methylcellulose, it is essential to consume it with at least 8 ounces (a full glass) of water or another fluid. Insufficient fluid intake may cause the product to swell and block the throat or esophagus, potentially leading to choking. Individuals with difficulty swallowing should not take this product. If symptoms such as chest pain, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, or breathing occur after taking the product, immediate medical attention should be sought. Common adverse reactions include flatulence and abdominal distension. In rare cases, intestinal obstruction may occur. There is limited information available regarding post-marketing experiences, drug interactions, and off-label uses of methylcellulose in both adult and pediatric populations. Methylcellulose is contraindicated in individuals who cannot swallow properly or who experience sudden changes in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks, abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting. If constipation persists for more than seven days or if rectal bleeding occurs, use should be discontinued, and a healthcare provider should be consulted, as these may indicate a more serious condition. The product is classified as a bulk-forming fiber laxative. Each caplet contains 500 mg of methylcellulose, along with other inactive ingredients such as croscarmellose sodium, dibasic calcium phosphate, and magnesium stearate. It is non-allergenic and provides additional dietary fiber without causing excessive gas. There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of methylcellulose during pregnancy, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, or in pediatric, geriatric, or immunocompromised patients. Similarly, there is no established guidance on its use in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment, or in specific gender or racial populations. Methylcellulose should be stored below 77°F (25°C) and protected from humidity. The container should be kept tightly closed to maintain product integrity. Patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding the use of alcohol while taking methylcellulose, as no established interaction has been documented. In case of overdose, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center is recommended immediately. The product is marketed under the brand name Citrucel® and is available in various forms, including caplets. It is promoted as a gentle and clinically proven effective fiber therapy for regularity, providing additional fiber to balance the diet without causing excess gas.
